title: CDP tab sovereignty: no cross-agent interference (campaign charter)
desc: Owner ruling 2026-09-05: in multi-tab multi-repo concurrent use, ANY case where AppBot disturbs a tab it was not addressed to, or is steered by whichever tab happens to be active, is a BUG to be exterminated. The charter: address by identity never by ambient state, never disturb what you do not own, recorded ownership is not enforced ownership, and prove it with a two-repo falsifier because a single-agent test cannot see this class.
steps: DECISION: TWO DIRECTIONS, BOTH ARE BUGS -- owner ruling 2026-09-05, and this is the whole charter. WHEN: you are judging any report about AppBot behaving oddly while more than one agent, tab or repo is live. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-command-guide for the command surface, then classify the report into one of exactly two directions and treat EITHER as a defect to be exterminated rather than a quirk to be worked around -- (A) OUTBOUND, AppBot touches a tab or window it was not addressed to: it resizes, moves, focuses, navigates, closes, or writes into something another agent or the owner is using; (B) INBOUND, AppBot is steered by ambient state instead of by its own address: it acts on whatever tab is active, foreground, first in a list, or most recently used, so another agent's activity changes where its command lands. WHY: the owner's words were that anything where AppBot affects the current active tab, or is interfered with by it, is a bug to be killed. The two directions look unrelated in a bug report -- one is "it moved my window", the other is "my command went to the wrong page" -- but they are one defect wearing two faces: a command that does not carry a tab IDENTITY must fall back on ambient state, and ambient state is exactly what other agents change.

DECISION: THE INVARIANT IS ADDRESS BY IDENTITY, NEVER BY AMBIENT STATE. WHEN: you are writing or reviewing any code path that has to decide WHICH tab or window to act on. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the reuse contract, then require that the target be named by a stable identity the caller supplied or claimed -- a CDP target id, a grap carrying an hwnd, a ledger entry keyed to this caller -- and REFUSE when identity cannot be established. Never resolve by active window, foreground window, first match, most recent, or "the only one running". WHY: a fallback to ambient state is not a convenience, it is the bug. Under one agent it is invisible because ambient happens to be correct; the moment a second agent exists it silently becomes wrong, and it stays silent because both answers are well-formed tabs. A guard that cannot answer NO is not a guard -- if the identity is unknown, the correct behaviour is to fail loudly, not to guess.

DECISION: NEVER DISTURB WHAT YOU DO NOT OWN, and placement counts as disturbance. APPLIED 2026-09-10: ChromeLauncher.LaunchPreparation.cs TryReuseExistingChromeAsync's any-running-Chrome fallthrough branch had no try-catch around FindRunningChromePort/IsPortActiveAsync, so a throw there could propagate instead of falling through to a fresh launch -- wrapped it to match the owned-Chrome branch above, which already degrades safely on any exception. WHEN: any code path calls SetForegroundWindow, MoveWindow, SetWindowPos, a resize, a tab activate, or a navigate on a window it did not itself create for this command. HOW: run wkappbot skill read standard-chrome-window for the placement contract, then gate every such call on ownership of THAT window and make the ungated path an error rather than a default. WHY: measured and reported by the owner. wkappbot ask drives the web AIs through CDP and resizes the Chrome OUTER WINDOW to 804x710 and drags it beside the calling terminal on EVERY invocation, to whatever Chrome window it attaches to -- including one the owner is reading in. His words were that it must stop shrinking his tab size as it pleases. That is direction (A) exactly: a command doing legitimate work while trampling a window it was never addressed to.

DECISION: RECORDED OWNERSHIP IS NOT ENFORCED OWNERSHIP, and this repo currently records without enforcing. WHEN: you are about to trust that per-window ownership protects concurrent agents, or you are asked why a tab opened in another repo's window. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab, then grep the tree for call sites of the ownership LOOKUP, not for the ledger writes -- writes at every launch site prove nothing if nothing reads them. Verify by what the system REFUSES: two repos, two commands, and the second must not land in the first's window. WHY: the 2026-08-30 renewal deliberately replaced per-folder profile isolation with per-window ownership, which is a sound design, but only the RECORDING half landed. The lookup has no callers, so the launch path falls through to finding any running Chrome on the shared profile, and the owner reported exactly that on 2026-09-03: a tab opening inside another repo's window. Wire the lookup BEFORE the refusal, because refusing before lookup works locks the owner out of his own running browser.

DECISION: A COMPARISON WHOSE TWO SIDES HAVE BECOME EQUAL DOES NOT FAIL LOUDLY -- IT STARTS RETURNING TRUE FOR EVERYONE. WHEN: a design retires an identity proxy, such as a per-repo port or a per-repo profile folder, and you are deciding what else to check. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec, then grep for every test that COMPARED against the retired proxy rather than every use of it, since a comparison that silently becomes trivially true raises no error and produces no log line. WHY: two instances were found this way after the port and profile renewals, and the assumption is that more remain. The same shape appears wherever a scope collapses: an anchor window that falls back to the desktop window is shared by every process, and a pipe or lock named without a per-instance component is shared by every caller -- in each case the identity check still runs, still passes, and no longer discriminates.

HOWTO: PROVE INTERFERENCE THE ONLY WAY THAT COUNTS -- TWO REPOS, TWO AGENTS, ONE OBSERVATION. WHEN: you are verifying any fix in this campaign, or triaging a report you cannot reproduce alone. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto, then build the falsifier as a PAIR: open a tab from repo A, note its target id and its window geometry, then run the same command from repo B and re-check A -- A's tab must still exist, still be at the same size and position, still be on the same URL, and still be the tab A's next command reaches. A single-agent test cannot see any defect in this class, and that is precisely why the class survived. Record the BEFORE numbers, because the failure mode is a value that changed quietly rather than an error that was raised.

DECISION: TREAT SILENCE AS THE SYMPTOM, NOT THE ABSENCE OF ONE. WHEN: triaging a report in this class, or closing one as not-reproducible. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto and ask what the caller would OBSERVE -- in this class the answer is usually a well-formed result from the wrong tab, which is indistinguishable from success. So require a positive control: show the check detecting a KNOWN interference before accepting its report that there is none. WHY: every defect in this family produces valid-looking output. A command that read another agent's page returns a page. A window that was moved is still a window. Nothing throws, nothing logs, and the only evidence is a value someone happened to remember from before.

NAVIGATION: this skill is the CHARTER for the multi-tab multi-repo interference campaign; the operational detail lives with the tools it governs. WHEN: you have classified a report as belonging to this campaign and need the mechanics. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-command-guide for the command surface and port discipline, wkappbot skill read standard-chrome-window for window placement and what may be moved, wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the reuse and ownership path, and wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec for why the profile is shared and what that removed. WHY: this core holds only the decision rules -- what counts as a violation and what must be true instead -- so that it stays short enough to be read before every triage, while the per-tool mechanics stay where a maintainer of that tool will meet them.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- THE TAB-HOLDER PROCESS MUST BE SEPARATED PER WORKING FOLDER, and this closes a design conflict that had been standing open. WHEN: you are touching the Chrome launch path, the user-data-dir, or any plan that assumes one browser instance serves every repo. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec for what the shared profile bought and what it cost, then treat per-CWD process separation as the target state and the shared single instance as the defect -- the owner's words were that the tab-holder process not being separated per working folder, so they interfere freely, is itself a bug to exterminate. WHY, AND THE COST MUST BE SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: Chrome starts a second process only for a DIFFERENT user-data-dir, so per-folder processes require per-folder profiles, and per-folder profiles are exactly what the 2026-08-30 renewal removed in order to stop saved passwords and cookies vanishing when a folder name changed. The two goals are reachable together only if credentials are shared by a mechanism other than the profile folder, which is what the cookie auto-sync path exists for. So the operation is not simply reverting the renewal -- it is separating the PROCESSES while keeping the CREDENTIALS shared, and any plan that separates profiles without carrying credentials across will re-open the login-loss bug the renewal was written to close. This ruling supersedes the OWNER DECISION OWED entry in the project CLAUDE.md, which recorded that the caller-window ruling and the shared profile could not both hold.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05, second half -- THE WORKING FOLDER IS THE IDENTITY, AND THE PORT IS NOT. WHEN: you are writing or reviewing the reuse rule that decides whether to attach to an existing Chrome or start a new one, and whenever you are tempted to treat a listening debug port as proof that the right browser is already up. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the current reuse path, then key reuse on the WORKING FOLDER and never on the port -- if the folder's derived port is already held by a DIFFERENT folder's holder, take another port and start that folder's own process; do not attach. Each working folder gets its own tab-holder process AND its own window LAYOUT, launched and managed separately -- the owner named layout explicitly alongside process, so geometry is per-folder state, not a global the last caller wins. WHY: the owner's words were that the port using the same number is likewise, meaning the port number changes nothing about the separation requirement. That is the same shape as this skill's rule about a comparison whose two sides became equal: the port was adopted as an identity PROXY, and a reuse rule reading 'a port is listening, therefore this is my browser' silently stops discriminating the moment two folders derive into the same block -- which is precisely how a tab from one repo lands in another repo's window. Two processes cannot bind one debug port, so the correct behaviour when the derived port is taken by a foreign holder is to MOVE, not to merge; merging is the defect wearing the disguise of reuse.

VERIFIED 2026-09-05 -- THE MECHANICAL ROOT OF THE OWNER'S SYMPTOM IS THAT A PER-FOLDER TAB-HOLDER CANNOT EXIST TODAY, and two long-standing claims in this repo's notes are wrong. WHEN: you begin the per-folder separation work, or you are about to trust a Pending line about ports or ownership call sites. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec, then verify these four by grep yourself before planning anything, because two of them were recorded wrongly and stayed wrong for days. (1) All four overloads of GetDefaultUserDataDir return one shared folder, chrome-profiles/appbot -- ChromeLauncher.UserDataDir.cs lines 36, 49 and 76 -- and Chrome will not start a second process on one profile: it hands the URL to the running singleton and exits, so ONE tab-holder for the whole machine is the design, not an accident. (2) The port is now FIXED at 9300, not a four-port block -- UserDataDir.cs line 83, commit 32e597d017 -- so every folder derives the SAME number, which makes the owner's remark that the port being the same number changes nothing a literal description of the present state rather than a hypothetical. (3) FindChromeOwnedByCallerAsync has ONE call site, WebCommands.Part3.OwnershipGate.cs line 48, not zero as the project CLAUDE.md Pending still says; the file's own header records that the Pending line is stale. What is unwired is the REFUSAL, IsWindowOwnedBy, with zero call sites and deliberately so. (4) Three shared files are written with no lock at all -- chrome_window_ownership_{hash}.txt via File.WriteAllLines as a whole-file rewrite, cdp_port_{hash}.txt via File.WriteAllText, and the profile's Cookies, Login Data and Local State shared machine-wide -- so concurrent agents lose each other's entries silently. WHY THIS ORDERS THE WORK: the separation is not a matter of adding a guard to the launch path, it is a profile-identity change, and every guard added above the singleton is decoration until a second process can exist at all.

RESULT: THE SIX TARGETS, with file and line, and their status as of 2026-09-05 -- this is the campaign's kill list and it lives here so a successor does not re-derive it. WHEN: you pick up this campaign, or you are triaging a new interference report and want to know whether it is already known. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the reuse path these all sit on, then work the list in the order given, because target 1 is one line and target 5 is the one that must not be done first. (1) KILLED, awaiting live proof: csharp/src/WKAppBot.CLI/CdpTabManager.cs had Url.Contains(expectedHost) at THREE sites, not the two a survey reported -- :132 CreateShared, :167 ConnectAndResolveTab, and :60 ValidateAsync, which the survey missed and which is the worst of them because it declares a drifted tab healthy whenever the URL merely contains the host, so recovery never fires. All three now call HostEquals in the new CdpTabManager.HostMatch.cs, which parses the URL and compares hosts for EQUALITY and returns false for anything unparseable or hostless. (2) OPEN: the sandbox key is command plus subcommand plus a four-byte SHA256 of the caller CWD, so two agents in one repo calling one service get an IDENTICAL key and share a tab. (3) OPEN: AskTargetRegistry saves every agent's tab to one runtime/ask_targets.json with File.WriteAllText and no lock, so concurrent registration loses an entry and the loser creates another tab. (4) OPEN: on a registry miss the code adopts an existing tab by identity match, so two agents adopt one tab under different keys. (5) OPEN BUT ORDERED LAST: the ownership LOOKUP is wired -- one call site at WebCommands.Part3.OwnershipGate.cs:48 -- while the REFUSAL IsWindowOwnedBy has zero call sites deliberately; wiring refusal before the lookup is proven to answer would lock the owner out of his own browser. (6) OPEN: ask resizes the Chrome outer window to 804x710 and drags it beside the terminal on every call, AskCommands.CallerPlacement.cs:203, to whatever window it attached to. WHY THE ORDER: 1 was a single line with a security edge, 2 through 4 are the concurrency core, and 6 is the one the owner feels daily -- but 5 is last because it is the only one that can make things worse if rushed.

NAVIGATION: this core is the T1 CHARTER of a three-tier cluster and holds only what counts as a violation and what must be true instead. WHEN: you have classified a report as belonging to this campaign, or you are picking the work up cold and need either the procedures or the current target status. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference-howto for what to RUN, which carries the owner's five acceptance requirements, the two-repo falsifier that a single-agent test cannot replace, how to test a host match by what it REFUSES, why to grep for the pattern rather than trust a survey's list of sites, and why a refusal must never land before its lookup is proven; and run wkappbot skill read cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference-ref for the dated evidence, which carries the six targets with file and line and their status, the survey that found two substring sites where there were three, the two claims in this repo's own notes that grep proved wrong, and the mechanical root that a per-folder tab-holder cannot exist under one shared profile. WHY: this campaign generates measurements faster than it generates rules, and a charter that absorbs every measurement stops being readable at the moment someone needs it most, which is mid-triage with the owner waiting.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- AN UNDER-SPECIFIED GRAP IS AN ERROR, NOT A PUZZLE TO SOLVE. WHEN: any CDP or tab-addressed command receives a grap that names only the Chrome PROCESS, or carries no tab-discriminating information at all. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference-howto for the acceptance requirements, then REFUSE with an error naming what was missing, rather than resolving the ambiguity by picking the active, the foreground, the first or the most recent tab. The owner's words: if the intelligence writes the action-build grap badly it is fine to block it with an error -- specifically when it writes only the Chrome process, or when there is not one piece of tab-distinguishing information. WHY THIS IS THE SAME RULE AS THE CHARTER AND NOT A NEW ONE: this core already forbids resolving by ambient state, and a bare process grap leaves NOTHING BUT ambient state to resolve by, so today it silently resolves to whichever tab happens to be there -- another agent's, or the one the owner is reading. The refusal is also the cheapest possible fix for the whole campaign, because it converts a silent wrong answer into a loud one at the exact moment the caller could still say which tab it meant. AND IT COSTS THE CALLER NOTHING IT SHOULD HAVE HAD: a caller that genuinely owns a tab already knows its target id or its own window, so only a caller that was going to guess is refused.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- PROTECTION IS GRANTED IN PROPORTION TO THE DISCRIMINATION SUPPLIED, and this is the campaign's central contract. WHEN: you are designing tab resolution, writing a grap, or deciding whether a request is well-formed enough to serve at all. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference-howto for the acceptance requirements, then implement FOUR TIERS rather than a yes-or-no gate -- DOMAIN ONLY is served with exactly ONE tab allowed for that domain, so a second caller offering only the same domain must supply more or be refused; TITLE or similar added narrows it further and the guarantee narrows with it; DOWN TO THE A11Y NODE is the highest service level and the one to recommend in documentation and examples; and NOTHING that could distinguish a tab, a bare Chrome process with no domain and no title, is REFUSED with an error naming what was missing. WHY: this is the owner's design and it is better than the binary refusal I had written, because it makes the caller's PRECISION the unit of account -- a vague grap is not punished arbitrarily, it simply receives the weak guarantee it asked for, while a precise grap earns a strong one. It also makes collision impossible to reach silently: two callers can only land on one tab by both being vague, and vagueness is exactly the case the tiers refuse. The owner's words were that a careless grap which cannot prevent collision gets service denied.

TODO: wire BrowserWindowBelongsToAnotherCaller (A11yCommand.FindSetup.cs:113, currently only self-called) into a real a11y action entry point as an ownership-refusal guard -- landed public but inert; contract: pick the lowest-risk single call site, add a guard clause following the existing refusal pattern, verify with a small diff and a live grep confirming a new call site. RESULT: the adoption rule now lives in one module, AskCommands.Entry.TabClaim.cs, and the host keeps a single call. WHEN: you are implementing or reviewing any tab-adoption path, or a fat-source guard refuses a change whose bulk is the comment explaining a trap. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-tab-sovereignty-no-cross-agent-interference-howto for the acceptance requirements, then put the RULE and its reasoning in the module and leave the caller one line -- ClaimedTabTargetIds returns every targetId registered under any key, and FirstAdoptableTab returns the first identity-matching tab that nobody has claimed, or null. WHY: two forces pushed the same way. The campaign needs the rule stated once rather than inlined at each caller, since identity matching is not ownership and every site that forgets that recreates the two-owners-one-tab defect. And fat-source-growth refused the inline version twice, correctly -- the growth was mostly the comment recording why a claim cannot become a leak, which is the next reader's study-lock pass and must not be deleted to satisfy a guard. Extracting keeps the explanation and satisfies the guard in the same move, and the host shrinks instead of growing.

DECISION: THE SECOND TAB HOLDER IS OPENED THROUGH THE FIRST ONE, AND THE REPOSITORY HINT IS STAMPED INTO ITS IDENTITY AT THAT MOMENT -- owner ruling 2026-09-05, and it is the design the whole campaign now rests on. WHEN: you are about to conclude that per-working-folder browser separation is impossible because a browser runs one process per profile and a second process will not start. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec for the settled profile ruling, then create the new window through the EXISTING debugging connection with the protocol's new-window flag rather than by launching a second browser, and stamp the folder hint onto the window as it is created. WHY THIS SURVIVES WHAT THE EARLIER PROPOSALS DID NOT: a caller window handle is recycled by the operating system and a terminal closed and reopened is a different console, so both DERIVE identity from something outside the window and both go stale -- that objection is what killed keying ownership on the caller handle. A stamp lives ON the window, so it survives a recycled handle, a restarted terminal and a page navigating away. THE HALF THAT MAKES IT FINDABLE, confirmed by reading WindowFinder.cs lines 122-130 rather than by recollection: the window-pattern matcher accepts a title field matched as a SUBSTRING with glob and regex support, so a marker that reaches a window title is locatable by the accessibility find command with no new matcher. THE INVARIANT THE MATCHER MUST HOLD: a window carrying NO hint returns false, never true -- a window that cannot prove it belongs to a folder does not belong to it, and every instinct to allow an unknown window just this once reopens the whole hole. VERIFY THIS MODULE BY WHAT IT REFUSES: an unstamped window and a window stamped for a DIFFERENT folder must both be rejected before any positive case is demonstrated.

DECISION: THE UNIT OF SEPARATION IS THE TAB, NOT THE WINDOW -- owner ruling 2026-09-05, superseding step 23's tab-holder-window design within the same hour; his words were not to let it open new windows as it pleases, just open a new tab. WHEN: you are about to create a browser WINDOW for a working folder, or to treat the broken new-window path as a blocker on this campaign. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-open-reuse-existing-chrome-tab for the reuse-then-new-tab path that is already the default, and make the new-window flag REFUSE cleanly rather than attempt creation -- a refusal naming the tab alternative, never a hang. WHY: the earlier design was retired by measurement rather than by argument. The new-window path was run live on port 9300 and creates NOTHING -- one real window before the call and the same one after; it attached to whatever target was CURRENTLY ACTIVE, the owner's own login page, and timed out in Runtime.enable after 15002ms with rc=1, filed as a suggest with a three-line reproduction. THE ROOT IS THE WRONG ENDPOINT, and it generalises: creating a target is a BROWSER-level operation, so it belongs on the browser WebSocket from /json/version, not on a PAGE target -- attaching to a page drags in that page's domain-enable handshake, and cdp-evalasync-retry-policy step 22 records that the ENTIRE domain-enable family hangs against a frozen or dialog-blocked renderer. Asking a page to make a window is asking the wrong object. TWO CONSEQUENCES OUTLIVE THE BUG. Tab grain removes the dependency on that path, leaves the owner's window layout untouched, and lands on machinery this campaign already built -- host equality, the claimed-tab check, the cross-process registry mutex -- while a tab already carries a unique never-reused target id, so the window stamp is no longer needed for per-folder identity and remains only for deciding which WINDOW may be moved. And what tab grain COSTS: a tab switch is VISIBLE to the owner where a background tab in another window is not, so dropping to tabs moves the active-tab interference risk rather than removing it. The mitigation has the same shape as the placement gate -- never call activateTarget or bringToFront on a window this caller does not own. Verified 2026-09-05 that neither appears as a live call in the CLI; keep it that way.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- CHECK FOR THE DIALOG BROKER BEFORE AND AFTER EVERY CDP EXCHANGE, AND EMIT THE ACCESSIBILITY INFORMATION WHEN ONE IS FOUND; his words were that for concurrent CDP the thing to watch is verifying the broker's presence before and after the exchange, then error-handling and surfacing the a11y information. WHEN: you are adding or reviewing any CDP call that will run while other agents or the owner share the browser, which under one shared profile is every call. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-evalasync-retry-policy for the existing fast-fail contract, then require THREE things of each exchange -- a pre-check that refuses in about 0ms on an already-open dialog, a POST-check on the SUCCESS path, and an error carrying what the accessibility layer can see rather than a bare timeout. WHY: the owner named the cost in one sentence -- without this the user flounders, asking why CDP is not working and why it has been stuck for ten minutes. A hang with no stated cause makes a person doubt the TOOL when the real answer, a dialog nobody mentioned, is sitting on screen the whole time; the error message is the entire difference between a ten-minute mystery and a five-second fix. THE POST-CHECK IS THE NEW HALF AND CONCURRENCY IS WHAT MAKES IT NECESSARY: a single agent can assume nothing appears between its own send and its own receive, so a pre-check suffices; with several agents on one browser another party can raise a dialog MID-EXCHANGE and the call may still return a well-formed answer computed against a page that is now blocked -- this charter's silence-is-the-symptom rule in its purest form. MEASURED THE SAME DAY and the gap is larger than expected: all four ThrowIfDialogBlocking call sites live in EvalAsync at CdpClient.Actions.cs lines 28, 66, 104 and 124, one upfront and three inside timeout and retry catch paths, so the check runs BEFORE an exchange and AFTER a FAILURE and never after a success; and it exists ONLY in EvalAsync, leaving the generic command path -- navigate, input dispatch, target operations -- entirely unguarded. THE ACCESSIBILITY HALF IS NOT DECORATION: cdp-evalasync-retry-policy step 22 measured that the ENTIRE domain-enable family hangs against a dialog-blocked renderer, so at the exact moment the caller most needs to know what is on screen CDP cannot tell it and only the OS accessibility tree can.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- THE CONSOLE AXIS BECOMES A FIELD NAMED con CARRYING A CONSOLE-INFO STRING, SUBSTRING-MATCHED, and it beats the numeric console id proposed first. WHEN: you are adding a belonging axis to the window-pattern language, or wondering why a caller cannot say which console a window belongs to. HOW: run wkappbot skill read a11y-find for the field vocabulary and the FOCUS TARGET INFO output contract, then add con alongside title, proc and cls as a SUBSTRING field rather than alongside pid and cid as a numeric one, and never overload cid, which already means CONTROL id and is compared against a control identifier. WHY: Article 1 of the exec constitution says the console IS the identity, but Article 3B records that a VS Code integrated terminal is ITSELF a pseudo-console SHARED across the whole terminal tab -- so inside an editor a single console id covers the human's own shell AND every agent-spawned child at once, and the axis that discriminates cleanly in a real terminal stops discriminating exactly where it is needed most. A STRING carries the console axis and the session evidence together, so one field answers both questions and a short substring stays a broad filter while a longer one narrows; a number can only ever answer one. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT SURVIVE A DETACHED SPAWN: an environment variable is INHERITED by a child even when the parent chain is severed, and Article 3B records that severing as deliberate, with five live daemons measured 2026-08-20 having no parent at all -- so inherited evidence works where derived evidence fails. WHAT I GOT WRONG AND HE CORRECTED: I framed it as caller WINDOW HANDLE versus process id and recommended the id; both are DERIVED and both go stale, and reframing it as a string field dissolves the comparison rather than settling it. CROSS: the folder marker landed the same day is the second axis, stamped ON the window so it survives a terminal restart, and Article 3 requires two agreeing axes while refusing any single one.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- SAME WORKING FOLDER BUT A DIFFERENT CALLER WINDOW IS SOMEONE ELSE'S, so the folder axis alone never establishes ownership. WHEN: you are about to treat a folder match as proof that a window or tab is yours, or you are reviewing the folder marker landed the same day. HOW: run wkappbot skill read exec-console-binding-constitution for Article 3, which already requires two agreeing axes and refuses any single one, then require the ownership ledger to agree BEFORE acting -- it is keyed on the caller window handle against the window id, so it is exactly the second axis this ruling demands, and it already exists. WHY: two intelligences working the SAME repository is the ordinary case here, not the exotic one, and under a folder-only test both of their windows match each other's queries -- the folder identifies the PROJECT while the caller window identifies the AGENT, and only the pair identifies a session. CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR BY THE OWNER, and the correction makes the design simpler rather than harder -- THE TWO AXES SIT AT DIFFERENT LAYERS, they do not both apply to the same object. A TAB HOLDER, meaning the window, is keyed by FOLDER and is SHARED: two agents working the same repository are meant to share one holder, and that is correct behaviour rather than a leak. A TAB is keyed by the CALLER WINDOW and is PRIVATE: another agent's tab stays off limits even inside a shared holder. So the folder marker shipped today is COMPLETE FOR ITS LAYER and is not missing an axis; the caller-window axis belongs one level down, at the tab, where the address fragment already carries it. This also explains the owner's original report exactly: a tab appearing in ANOTHER REPOSITORY's window was wrong because the HOLDER was wrong, while two agents sharing one repository's holder was never the fault. THE LAYERS THIS SETTLES, and both already exist rather than needing invention: a WINDOW carries a Win32 property, which is where the folder hash lives, while a TAB has no window handle at all and is marked instead by a fragment appended to its address -- CdpClient.TabManagement3.cs line 82 builds it, and eight sites already skip a tab carrying one. So the answer to per-tab attribution is to put the caller identity in that fragment, never to reach for a window property a tab cannot have.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05, FINAL ON THIS QUESTION -- ONE HOLDER PER CALLER WINDOW, AND THE WORKING-FOLDER CONCEPT IS BANISHED FROM THE BROWSER WORLD ENTIRELY. WHEN: you meet the folder marker landed earlier the same day, or you are tempted to reintroduce a per-folder identity for windows or tabs. HOW: run wkappbot skill read exec-console-binding-constitution and read Article 1, which states in as many words that the console IS the identity and the working folder is NOT -- the folder marker was in tension with that article from the moment it shipped, and this ruling restores the constitution rather than departing from it. WHY: a holder owned by ONE caller window collapses two enforcement layers into one, and every failure measured this session was of the same shape -- a check present at one layer and missing at another, the reaper guarded in one of its two close loops, the hint suppressed at one of three emission sites, the byte counter incremented at one of four write sites. If the whole holder belongs to me then every tab in it does too, so a single window-level refusal replaces a check at every tab operation. It also dissolves the owner's original complaint outright: nobody else can move or resize a window that is nobody else's. TWO COSTS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY, recorded so they are not later mistaken for defects. More browser windows exist, one per live caller; the idle-tab reaper already recovers empty ones. And a caller window handle does not survive a terminal restart, so an old holder is orphaned as an empty window while a new one opens -- a folder key would have survived that, and this is the one thing given up. THE ONE PIECE THAT MUST SURVIVE THE REMOVAL: the unknown-field validation currently lives in the folder module and has nothing to do with folders. It is what makes a bad pattern refuse OUT LOUD instead of silently widening, so it changes house rather than dying with the folder concept.

VERIFIED: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- THE OWNER USES EDGE. CHROME IS THE AGENTS' BROWSER, and an inherited assumption to the contrary blocked live verification for a whole session. WHEN: you are about to defer a live browser test because the owner might be using the browser, or you are weighing how much a new Chrome window costs his desktop. HOW: run wkappbot skill read cdp-command-guide for the port discipline that still applies, then TEST FREELY IN CHROME -- open windows, close tabs, move geometry -- while treating any Edge window as untouchable. Never verify by asking; his words were that Chrome is for the agents alone. WHY THIS COST SO MUCH: the predecessor letter recorded its two-window falsifier as UNRUN because the owner was using the browser, this session inherited that sentence as fact, and every live proof in the campaign was postponed on it. The two-window proof, the new-window path, the placement refusal and the per-caller holder demonstration were ALL deferred for a reason that was never true. IT ALSO SKEWED A DESIGN DECISION: choosing one holder per caller window over a shared per-folder holder, the cost entered against it was extra windows cluttering a contested desktop -- and that cost is near zero once the browser is not his. AN INHERITED CONSTRAINT IS A CLAIM LIKE ANY OTHER: it arrives in a letter with no evidence attached, it silently shapes every plan downstream, and it is cheaper to ask about once than to route around for a day.

DECISION: OWNER RULING 2026-09-05 -- TOUCHING ANOTHER CALLER'S WINDOW REQUIRES AN EXTRA OPTION NAMING THAT CALLER'S WINDOW HANDLE, and it should be deliberately awkward. WHEN: you are adding any verb that could act on a window this caller did not create, or reviewing one that currently just works. HOW: run wkappbot skill read exec-console-binding-constitution for Article 7, which already demands defence in layers, then require the caller to pass the TARGET caller's window handle explicitly -- a hex handle typed by hand, never a wildcard, never a filter that happens to select one window, and never an implicit fall-through to whatever was found. Print one line naming the target and the layer that permitted it. WHY: Article 7 already says an explicit named target is the layer that cannot be satisfied by accident, and this ruling supplies what NAMED means for a browser window. THE ELEGANT HALF, and it is why the two rules belong together: Article 8B puts every non-belonging window in an OTHER MATCHES section at the bottom carrying its grap, so a caller who legitimately needs a foreign window CAN discover its handle -- and must then copy it deliberately into the command. The discovery path stays open while the accidental path closes, which is exactly the asymmetry a safety layer wants. AND IT COSTS THE HONEST CALLER NOTHING: an agent acting on its own window already has its own handle and never sees this gate; only a caller that was about to reach across meets it. THE MEASURED CONTEXT: this desktop routinely carries browsers nobody claims -- a third Chrome process on an unrelated page was found during the same session, belonging to neither the owner nor this session -- so reaching across is a real act with a real victim, not a hypothetical.

VERIFIED: Ownership caller resolution wired 2026-09-06. WHEN: ChromeLauncher.OwnershipCallerHwnd replaces direct CallerHwndForPlacement reads at 5 ownership sites. HOW: wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto to verify the resolver correctly handles all paths (env var, IPC, pipe PID walk, latched value). WHY: The direct CallerHwndForPlacement read only sees IPC field, missing 4 resolution sources that placement already used, causing ownership to always record/lookup zero from non-launcher paths.

BUG: the grap wildcard star-Chrome-star selects the OWNER'S MICROSOFT EDGE window, because Edge carries the same Win32 class Chrome_WidgetWin_1 and the wildcard matches the CLASS, not the process. WHEN: any a11y command aimed at the appbot browser, and especially the tab-portal form that a11y --help itself recommends. HOW: run wkappbot skill read standard-chrome-window for the window-versus-tab rules, then address the browser by PROCESS -- a grap of the shape proc chrome plus a URL suffix -- and never by a class-name wildcard. Verify by reading the line the tool marks as SELECTED, not the list: the marker is a greater-than sign before the entry. WHY: measured 2026-09-06 on staging v7.9.207. The command a11y read star-Chrome-star hash example.com with --nth 1 printed as its chosen target a Microsoft Edge window at hwnd 00790728, 1955x1793, ahead of every real chrome.exe window in the same list. The owner uses Edge as his personal browser, so the form the help text recommends aims automation at the one browser this charter exists to protect. Switching the same command to a proc-scoped grap excluded Edge cleanly and listed only chrome.exe windows, which is the fix and also the proof. TWO FOLLOW-ONS worth knowing before you trust a window list here: the first proc-scoped match was a 282x101 Chrome TRANSLATE BUBBLE rather than a page, so --nth 1 is not the page even after the process is right; and counting windows with Get-Process is useless because Chrome is ONE process with many windows, so MainWindowHandle reports exactly one. Filed as a suggest 2026-09-06.

INCIDENT: MY OWN FIX CAUSED THE EXACT INTERFERENCE THIS CHARTER FORBIDS -- a blanket ledger wipe at launch handed one agent another agent's window. WHEN: any change that CLEARS or REBUILDS shared ownership state, and any fix justified by a finding that was later retracted. HOW: run wkappbot skill read chrome-profile-identity-shared-credentials-spec for the ledger-lifetime rules, then never clear SHARED state on a per-caller event -- a launch belongs to ONE caller, the ledger belongs to ALL of them. If a lifetime bound is genuinely needed, stamp the browser instance on each ROW and treat a foreign-instance row as absent; a blanket wipe cannot distinguish stale from someone-else's. WHY: measured 2026-09-06 on staging v7.9.210, four calls, two callers. A1 caller 0x180276 got a new window and the ledger read exactly 0x180276 TAB 1585304012. A2 correctly reused. Then B1 caller 0x1A20710 ran, and the ledger read 0x1A20710 TAB 1585304012 -- A's row GONE and B recorded against 1585304012, which is A'S OWN windowId. B found no ownership, fell to the launch path, ClearOwnershipLedger wiped A's row, and B was then recorded against whatever window CDP considered current, which was A's. ONE AGENT OWNED ANOTHER AGENT'S WINDOW, caused by the very commit meant to protect ownership. TWO COMPOUNDING LESSONS. FIRST, the commit was written for a stale-row finding I RETRACTED hours earlier because the kill it relied on never happened -- A FIX BUILT ON A RETRACTED FINDING SHOULD BE REVERTED, NOT TUNED, because nothing it protects has ever been shown to exist. SECOND, the four-call falsifier is what caught it: A1 and A2 both PASSED and the damage only appeared at B1, so a two-call test on a single caller would have shipped this.

requirements.expect: the ownership LOOKUP call-site count; more than one file means the lookup is finally wired
Article 8B, the OTHER MATCHES section: a result belonging to nobody leaves the main set and prints one grap plus one title at the bottom -- this campaign's rendering law, already ruled 2026-08-27
the FOCUS / TARGET / INFO output contract and the AMB:N ambiguity signal this campaign's window addressing must speak, plus the WIDEN rule for a zero-result search
